help.packageFiles: Confirm that the SQL dump you plan to restore is present and that you also have the manifest, release notes, or operator notes that explain what was backed up. Without those files, you can restore the database but still lose context about paths, versions, or missing companion data.
help.mediaCopied: The SQL restore only recreates Fable records. It does not bring your EPUB, PDF, CBZ, CBR, or audiobook files onto the new host. Check this only after the target machine already has the full library media in the correct folders.
help.appDataReady: Fable also depends on mounted app-data such as generated images, thumbnails, and runtime files. Confirm that the destination app-data folder exists, is mounted into the container, and matches the path you entered above.
help.composeReady: You need the compose file, container config, or deployment notes that describe the MariaDB service name, volume mounts, and Fable paths. This is what lets you rebuild the environment in the same shape before importing the SQL dump.
help.versionReady: Make sure the destination Fable and MariaDB versions can safely consume this backup. If the target is older, newer in an incompatible way, or missing required migrations, the import can succeed technically but still leave the app unstable.
help.maintenanceReady: The restore should happen while writes are paused. Confirm you can stop scans, uploads, metadata edits, and any other background jobs so the database is not changing while the import is running.
